# Introduction

This document details the sensitivity analyses performed for the vitamin network meta analysis. The goal here is to 

1. Verify the correctness of our code as compared to other implementations (e.g., multinma)
  a. Within multinma, verify that fixed vs unrelated means do not fit better
  b. Within multinma, verify that node splitting does not change results
  c. Within multinma, examine outliers
2. Check the sensitivity and performance of the chosen Student's T distribution for the likelihood as compared to a Gaussian distributions
3. Compare changes to heterogenity and fit with a fully adjusted meta-regression


# Models analyzing depression outcome

## Comparison of Student's T to Gaussian likelihoods
We utilize Leave-One-Out cross-validation (LOO-CV) to compare the fit of models using a Student's T likelihood versus a Gaussian likelihood. The models are fitted using the `brms` package, and we assess the expected log predictive density (ELPD) for each model. These LOO-CV estimates are exact fits as the estimates are used for figures and tables in the main manuscript.

```{r, loo_est}

loo_l <- loo::loo_compare(
  list(
    mvt_l  = loo_low %>% vit$loo.vit_loo(),
    mvn_l  = loo_gauss_low %>% vit$loo.vit_loo(),
  )
)


loo_s <- loo::loo_compare(
  list(
    mvt_s  = loo_some %>% vit$loo.vit_loo(),
    mvn_s  = loo_gauss_some %>% vit$loo.vit_loo(),
    multinma = l_some
))



loo_h <- loo::loo_compare(
  list(
    mvt_h  = loo_high %>% vit$loo.vit_loo(),
    mvn_h  = loo_gauss_high %>% vit$loo.vit_loo(),
    multinma = l_all,
    metareg = b_l %>% vit$loo.vit_loo()
  )
)

```

```{r, meta_reg_compare tau}
bind_rows(
  posterior::as_draws_df(bias_reg, variable = "tau_y") %>%
    select(tau_y) %>% mutate(tau = tau_y,
                             model = "bias adjusted"),
  posterior::as_draws_df(fit_brms_def, variable = "tau") %>%
    select(tau) %>%
    mutate(model = "deficiency vs depressed"),
  posterior::as_draws_df(high_t, variable = "tau") %>%
    select(tau) %>%
    mutate(model = "simple model") 
) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = tau, fill = model)) +
  ggridges::geom_ridgeline(aes(y = model, 
                               height = ..density.., 
                               group = model),
                           stat = "density_ridges", scale = 0.25,
                           alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "bias adjusted" = "#e6550d",
    "deficiency v.s.\ndepressed" = "#31a354",
    "simple model" = "#6a51a3"
  )) +
  xlab(latex2exp::TeX("$\\tau$")) +
  ggtitle(latex2exp::TeX("Posterior distribution of study heterogeneity ($\\tau$) for all data")) +
  vit$theme_vit() 

```


## Analyzing fit of multinma models
```{r}
# check DC to see which fits better
  (dic_FE <- dic(fit_FE))
  (dic_RE <- dic(fit_RE)) # appears to fit better


  (dic_RE <- dic(fit_RE))
  (dic_UME <- dic(UME_RE)) # appears roughly the same
  
  # check heterogeneity
  summary(UME_RE, pars = "tau")
  summary(fit_RE, pars = "tau") # also roughly the same
  
  # check for differences 
  plot(dic_RE, dic_UME, show_uncertainty = FALSE) +
    xlab("Residual deviance - RE model") +
    ylab("Residual deviance - UME model")
  # appear mostly on line 
  
  as.data.frame(dic_RE) %>%
    arrange(desc(resdev)) %>%
    head(10) # large deviance obs but it appears to have low leverage....
  
  as.data.frame(dic_RE) %>%
    arrange(desc(leverage)) %>%
    head(10) # the large leverage obs have reasonable deviance
  
  summary(node_split_low)
  # tau about the same, no DIC change
  
  summary(node_split_some)
  # tau relatively the same, no DIC change
  
  summary(node_split_high)
  dic(fit_RE_all)
  
  #### Loo comparisons ####
l_all  <- loo::loo(d_fit_RE_all)
l_some <- loo::loo(d_fit_RE_some)
l_low  <- loo::loo(d_fit_RE)

l_brms_low  <- fit_brms_low  %>% loo::loo(., moment_match = TRUE) #vit$reloo.vitfit(., loo::loo(.))
l_brms_some <- fit_brms_some %>% loo::loo(., moment_match = TRUE) #%>% vit$reloo.vitfit(., loo::loo(.))
l_brms_high <- fit_brms_high %>% vit$reloo.vitfit(., loo::loo(.))

# check loo
loo::loo_compare(

)

# check if distribution is correct 
  {
    if(rlang::is_interactive()) {
      
      summary_fit_bias <- vit$summary_brms_nma(fit_bias, keep = c(".trt","bias") )
      
      if (!("d_fit_RE_bias" %in% ls())) {
        d_fit_RE_bias <- nma(vit$construct_nma_network(data), 
                             trt_effects = "random",
                             regression = ~ .trt*bias ,
                             prior_intercept = normal(scale = 1),
                             prior_reg = normal(0, .25),
                             prior_trt = normal(0, .5),
                             prior_het = half_normal(0.5),
                             cores = 4L,
                             seed = 1293696306,
                             control = list(max_treedepth = 15L)
        )
      }
      
      
      ot_x <- vit$contrasts(summary_fit_bias, "Antidepressant, D", "Antidepressant") %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% .$value
      ot_y <- posterior::as_draws_matrix(fit_ssri_low, variable = "b_main_.trtantidepressant_d")[,1]
      cat(sprintf("         ot between subset and re model for low-bias for antidepressant contrasts: %f", (approxOT::wasserstein(ot_x, ot_y, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 100)^2 - 
        0.5 * approxOT::wasserstein(ot_x, ot_x, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 1000)^2 - 
        0.5 * approxOT::wasserstein(ot_y, ot_y, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 1000)^2)))
      # for depression: 0.01504823 (somewhat different distribution), sinkhorn divergence; however, other methods below agree
      
      ot_x2 <- summary_fit_bias %>% filter(.trt == "D") %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% .$value
      ot_y2 <- posterior::as_draws_matrix(fit_low, variable = "b_main_.trtd")[,1]
      cat(sprintf("         ot between brms and multinma for low bias estimate of vitamin D: %f", approxOT::wasserstein(ot_x2, ot_y2, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 100)^2 - 
              0.5 * approxOT::wasserstein(ot_x2, ot_x2, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 1000)^2 - 
              0.5 * approxOT::wasserstein(ot_y2, ot_y2, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 1000)^2))
      # for depression 0.000168049 (almost same distribution), sinkhorn divergence
      ot_x3 <- summary_fit_bias %>% filter(.trt == "D") %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% .$value
      ot_y3 <- d_fit_RE_bias$stanfit %>% posterior::as_draws_matrix(variable = "d[D]") %>% .[,"d[D]"]
      print(approxOT::wasserstein(ot_x3, ot_y3, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 100)^2 - 
              0.5 * approxOT::wasserstein(ot_x3, ot_x3, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 1000)^2 - 
              0.5 * approxOT::wasserstein(ot_y3, ot_y3, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 1000)^2)
      # for depression (0.0007800334), comparing multinma to brms fits (also likelihood slightly different)
      
      ot_y4 <- d_fit_RE_bias$stanfit %>% posterior::as_draws_matrix(variable = "d[antidepressant, D]") %>% .[,"d[antidepressant, D]"] - d_fit_RE_bias$stanfit %>% posterior::as_draws_matrix(variable = "d[antidepressant]") %>% .[,"d[antidepressant]"]
      cat(sprintf("         ot between brms and multinma for antidepressant contrasts: %f", approxOT::wasserstein(ot_x, ot_y4, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 100)^2 - 
              0.5 * approxOT::wasserstein(ot_x, ot_x, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 1000)^2 - 
              0.5 * approxOT::wasserstein(ot_y4, ot_y4, p = 2, method = "sinkhorn", epsilon = 1, niter = 1000)^2))
      # for depression (0.001624), comparing multinma to brms fits
    } 
  }
```

## Comparison with multinma models

```{r}

l_low  <- vit$multinma_loo(fit_RE)
l_some <- vit$multinma_loo(fit_RE_some)
l_all  <- vit$multinma_loo(fit_RE_all)

loo_l_multinma <- loo::loo_compare(
  list(
    mvt_l  = loo_low %>% vit$loo.vit_loo(),
    multinma = l_low
  )
)


loo_s_multinma <- loo::loo_compare(
  list(
    mvt_s  = loo_some %>% vit$loo.vit_loo(),
    multinma = l_some
))



loo_h_multinma <- loo::loo_compare(
  list(
    mvt_h  = loo_high %>% vit$loo.vit_loo(),
    multinma = l_all
  )
)
```
